To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Local government was not deliberately excluded from the Australian Constitution. Rather, it was simply overlooked.
The Australian Constitution does not specifically mention local government, and it is not a Commonwealth power, but it does not specifically exclude it either.
local government was ‘left on theshelf’ by being denied a place in the AustralianConstitution.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Commonwealth has no constitutional power to intervene in local government affairs.

the Commonwealth Government has not been involved in local government, except for the Commonwealth Grants Commission, the Local Government Grants Commission and, in a limited way, the Commonwealth Employment Service.

the Commonwealth has no constitutional powers in relation to the administration of local government, but it has powers in relation to local government finance and the provision of services, and it has a role in local government reform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the absence of a constitutional basis for local government, the Commonwealth has been able to intervene in local government affairs, but that the Commonwealth has been reluctant to do so and has, in fact, been a reluctant participant in the development of local government.
, while there is a strong case for constitutional recognition, the current situation is satisfactory, and that there is no need for constitutional reform.

, despite the fact that local government was not specifically mentioned in the Australian Constitution, local government has been a key player in the development and implementation of Commonwealth policies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
local government is a state and territory matter, not a Commonwealth matter.
local government inAustralia has a limited range of functionscompared with most OECD countries, andthat it has been ‘kept in check’, in part, bybeing denied a place in the national polity.
the federal government has a limited role in the provision of local government services, and this role is largely confined to the provision of financial assistance.
